project.title: In-Store Customer Experience and Merchandising Refresh
project.objective: Improve in-store customer experience and product presentation to increase conversion and repeat visits across key product categories.
deliverables: Standardised product display layouts for top-selling categories
Customer guidance scripts for common enquiries and complaints
Weekly stock and facing checklist for sales floor staff
Simple aftersales and follow-up process for priority customers
Short training huddle plan for new merchandising standards
constraints: All changes must be implementable during normal shifts with no extra staffing
No changes that require store remodelling or new fixtures
Customer service scripts must comply with existing company policies
New routines must be testable in-store within 3 weeks
Stock handling must follow current safety and loss-prevention rules

risks.risk: New display standards slow down daily replenishment and cause delays on the shop floor.
risks.mitigation: Pilot layouts in one area, collect feedback from sales assistants, and simplify steps before full rollout.

risks.risk: Customer guidance scripts feel too rigid and reduce natural interaction.
risks.mitigation: Frame scripts as prompts, gather examples from staff, and allow adaptation within policy limits.

risks.risk: Inconsistent adoption of new checklists across shifts.
risks.mitigation: Create a simple checklist format, assign shift leads to sign off, and review completion weekly.

risks.risk: Stock availability issues undermine improved merchandising.
risks.mitigation: Align new displays with current stock levels and add a quick escalation rule for low-stock items.

themes.why_relevant: Sales assistants need clear, consistent ways to advise customers and suggest suitable products.
Organised, attractive displays help customers find items quickly and support higher sales.
Good displays fail if shelves are empty; staff must link merchandising with stock checks.
Simple follow-up routines can turn one-time buyers into repeat customers and reduce complaints.
New standards must fit into daily opening, peak, and closing routines across all shifts.

backlog.task: Map current customer questions and common issues at the sales counter and on the floor.
definition_of_done: At least 20 frequent questions or issues listed from recent shifts
Grouped into 5–7 themes (e.g. sizing, returns, product use)
Shared in channel and validated by at least two other sales assistants

backlog.task: Draft customer guidance prompts for top 5 product categories.
definition_of_done: For each category, 3–5 opening questions to identify needs are written
2–3 product recommendation examples per category documented
Checked against company policy and approved by store manager or delegate

backlog.task: Design a simple daily shelf presentation and cleanliness checklist.
definition_of_done: Checklist covers facing, gaps, price labels, and cleanliness
Takes less than 10 minutes per aisle to complete
Tested on one shift and adjusted based on feedback

backlog.task: Propose improved display layout for one high-traffic aisle.
definition_of_done: Current layout documented with quick photos or sketches
New layout plan created with clear product groupings and signage ideas
Store manager or visual merchandiser signs off pilot layout

backlog.task: Create a quick reference guide for handling refunds and exchanges at the counter.
definition_of_done: Key refund and exchange steps listed in order
Common edge cases (no receipt, damaged goods) included
Guide reviewed by customer service supervisor for policy compliance

backlog.task: Define a simple process to follow up with customers on special orders.
definition_of_done: Steps from order placement to pickup or delivery documented
Standard phrases for updates and delays drafted
Process tested with at least 3 recent special orders

backlog.task: Set up a weekly 10-minute huddle format to review displays and customer feedback.
definition_of_done: Agenda template created (wins, issues, quick fixes)
Timing agreed for each shift team
First huddle held and notes shared in channel

backlog.task: Identify top 10 products that need clearer information on the shelf.
definition_of_done: List of 10 products with reasons (e.g. complex use, frequent questions)
Suggested short info lines or icons drafted for each
Feasibility checked with store manager or visual merchandiser

backlog.task: Create a simple rotation plan for stock checks in high-loss or high-demand areas.
definition_of_done: High-risk aisles or categories identified
Rotation schedule defined by day and shift
Plan validated with inventory controller or equivalent

backlog.task: Document best practices for preventing shoplifting while maintaining good service.
definition_of_done: At least 5 practical behaviours listed (e.g. greeting, presence in aisles)
Aligned with existing loss-prevention rules
Shared with team and acknowledged by at least three colleagues

backlog.task: Prepare a short onboarding note for new sales assistants on the refreshed standards.
definition_of_done: 1-page summary of key routines (displays, checklists, scripts) written
Includes who to ask for help on each topic
Reviewed and approved by store manager or delegate

backlog.task: Collect before-and-after observations on customer behaviour in the pilot aisle.
definition_of_done: At least 3 days of observations before and 3 days after changes noted
Qualitative notes on questions, time spent, and visible confusion captured
Summary shared in channel with 2–3 improvement suggestions

threads_plan.thread_goal: Align on current pain points and prioritise focus areas for the refresh.
threads_plan.trigger: Kickoff message asking everyone to share top customer and merchandising issues.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Agree on the top 3 customer pain points to address first.
Select one high-traffic aisle to use as the initial pilot area.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Define customer guidance prompts and service scripts for key categories.
threads_plan.trigger: Post summarising frequent questions and asking for draft prompts and examples.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve a first version of customer guidance prompts for the top 5 categories.
Decide how strictly staff should follow the prompts versus adapting them.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Agree on the daily shelf presentation checklist and pilot aisle layout.
threads_plan.trigger: Message sharing draft checklist and layout proposal for feedback.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Sign off the daily shelf presentation and cleanliness checklist for use in all aisles.
Approve the pilot layout for the selected high-traffic aisle and set a start date.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Set routines for follow-up, stock checks, and weekly huddles.
threads_plan.trigger: Post proposing a simple follow-up flow, stock rotation plan, and huddle format.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Confirm the weekly huddle schedule and who leads on each shift.
Agree on the stock check rotation plan and priority areas.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Review pilot results and decide on adjustments before wider rollout.
threads_plan.trigger: Message sharing before-and-after observations from the pilot aisle.

channel_rituals: Start-of-shift async check-in where each assistant posts key focus for the shift.
End-of-day quick summary of notable customer feedback or display issues.
Weekly huddle notes posted as a short recap with any agreed changes.
Pilot review post at the end of each week summarising observations and next tweaks.
